chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

A man asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who performs all the circuits (of Tawaf) and combines them (praying two rak'ahs after one circuit or completing the prayer after multiple circuits). He said: 'No, [the correct way is] the circuit and two rak'ahs. And Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) combined [praying after multiple circuits] because he was performing Tawaf with Muhammad ibn Ibrahim due to the state of Taqiyya (dissimulation/prudence).'

And whoever combines between the circuits, it is disliked for him to conclude on an even number, and it is preferred that he concludes on an odd number, such as restricting himself to two circuits. For the best, when the state is as we mentioned, is to make that three circuits.
That is indicated by what he narrated:

key_terms.التَّقِيَّة: Taqiyya, dissimulation or prudence in religious practice
key_terms.الطَّوَاف: Tawaf, ritual circumambulation of the Kaaba
key_terms.الْأَسْبَاع: The circuits (plural of sab' or asb)
key_terms.يَقْرُنُ: He combines (referring to combining prayer with multiple circuits)

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred method for praying during Tawaf and how many circuits should one complete?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of Tawaf by distinguishing between the general recommendation to pray two rak'ahs after each circuit and the specific practice of Imam al-Rida (AS), who combined prayers due to *Taqiyya* (dissimulation) while with Muhammad ibn Ibrahim. It further establishes the preference for ending the ritual on an odd number of circuits (witr) rather than an even number (shuf), reflecting the broader Islamic aesthetic of balance and completion. This ruling underscores the flexibility in ritual practice based on context while maintaining a preferred normative standard.
